title: K-PACT: Kernel Planning for Adaptive Context Switching - A Framework for Clustering, Placement, and Prefetching in Spectrum Sensing
problem: Spectrum sensing applications require adaptive processing kernels with dynamic workload characteristics; static scheduling causes inefficient resource utilization and poor QoS.
motivation: Context-aware kernel scheduling improves throughput and latency in reconfigurable spectrum processing platforms; adaptive placement and prefetching reduce memory stalls.
method: K-PACT groups related spectrum processing steps together so they can share data already in fast memory. It watches which steps typically run one after another; when the processor switches between them (a context switch), it prefetches the next step's data. This keeps the data ready in fast memory instead of forcing the step to wait for data from slow storage.
key_novelty: Rather than using a fixed task schedule, dynamically prefetch the next task's data by learning which tasks usually follow each other, allowing related tasks to share data in fast memory.
contributions: Kernel clustering methodology for spectrum processing
Adaptive placement strategy based on data locality
Demonstrated improvements in throughput and latency for spectrum sensing
limitations: Analysis limited to abstract; specific spectrum sensing workloads and performance metrics not detailed.
primary_theme: adaptive kernel scheduling for spectrum sensing via clustering and prefetching
